NEW DELHI, MARCH 10

WATER-ICE ON the Moon could
be more prevalent than under-
stood earlier. A new analysis of
data from one of the instruments
aboard Chandrayaan-3 suggests
that there was a good probability
that water-ice was present in lo-
cations outside of the polar re-
gions of the Moon.
Using data from Chandra’s
Surface Thermophysical
Experiment (ChaSTE), scientists
at the Ahmedabad-based
Physical Research Laboratory
have shown that surface and
sub-surface temperaturesin the
higher latitudes of the Moon's
surface varied greatly witheven
very small changes in altitudes

over a short distance. Inclined ar-
eas in these latitudes that were
not directlyfacing theSuncould
have environments very similar
to the polar regions, and could
host water-ice below the surface.
The findings have been pub-
lished in the Communications

Nature publication.

articles.text:
WATER-ICE ON the Moon could be more prevalent than understood earlier. A new analysis of data from one of the instruments aboard Chandrayaan-3 suggests that there was a good probability that water-ice was present in locations outside of the polar regions of the Moon. Using data from Chandra's Surface Thermophysical Experiment (ChaSTE), scientists at the Ahmedabad-based Physical Research Laboratory have shown that surface and sub-surface temperaturesin the higher latitudes of the Moon's surface varied greatly witheven very small changes in altitudes

over a short distance. Inclined areas in these latitudes that were not directlyfacing theSuncould have environments very similar to the polar regions, and could host water-ice below the surface. The findings have been published in the Communications Earthand Environment joumal,a Nature publication.

HYDERABAD. MARCH 10

ON MARCH6, Mayaand Murphy,
two Belgian Malinois dogs that
belong to Kerala Police'scadaver
dog squad, briskty alighted from
an Indian Air Force chopper and
went straight to the Srisailam Left
Bank Canal(SLBC) tunnel near
Domalapenta of Telangana's
Nagarkumool district. Here, they
were handed the grim task of
finding the bodies of eight men
who were trapped in the

Telangana tunnel collapse that
occurred on February 22.
